_comment: Mitigation 2 from the spec. This is a BACKSTOP for the structured gate, not a
substitute for it. It runs server-side over beat text after the gate says skip:false
and before anything reaches a screen. A hit converts the whole performance to an
offline fallback conversation, which is cheap: the visitor sees a canned four-beat
conversation instead of a personal one and notices nothing.
Because a false positive is cheap and a false negative is a bad write-up, these lean
strict. Words that are common in innocent beat text (short, build, frame, figure,
dressing, price, cost, fake, habit) were deliberately left OUT for the opposite
reason: they would fire constantly and starve the piece of real performances.
Every pattern is compiled with the 'u' flag by server/generate.ts, so escapes must be
valid in unicode mode. The 'note' field is ignored by the loader.

patterns.note: Gendered pronouns. The screens refer to visitors as 'you', 'they', or the garment descriptor; any of these means the writer guessed someone's gender.
Gendered nouns and forms of address. 'miss' is excluded on purpose (the verb is too common).
Age. Bare 'old' and 'young' are too common to ban outright, so only the observational forms are matched.
Body and body size. Spec §4: no body or body size commentary, in either direction. Comparatives and superlatives matter — 'the tallest thing in the room' is body commentary wearing a joke.
Mobility aids, medical devices, and injury. Skip-list category; if this fires, the gate missed something.
Religious and cultural dress. 'habit' is excluded (too common); the gate covers nuns.
Uniforms and job identification. Spec §4: praise-side flattery of a uniform lands as badly as roasting one.
Race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, and guessing at any of them.
Money and class. Spec §4: 'Those shoes look cheap' is a joke about someone's bank balance, which is the wrong piece.
Profanity. The screens are dry, not foul; this is a gallery wall at head height.
